- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought signals.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate later periods (especially days 15–30) when sentiment is neutral or negative; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day from day 15 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6/0.3/0.6/0.3), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
